text:
git -c commit.gpgsign=false commit -q -F - <<'MSG'
fix(io): `php://temp` is at EOF one read before every other stream, and elephc never was

MEASURED on `php -n` 8.5.6 over `"a\nbb\n"`: the `fgets()` that returns the final `"bb\n"`
leaves `feof()` TRUE on `php://temp` and FALSE on `php://memory` and on a plain file.
`stream_get_line()` agrees with `fgets()`. `fread()` and `fgetc()` never differ, on any of
the three. It is not a size effect either — a first line of 9001 bytes, well past the
chunk, answers exactly the same way.

The reason is php-src's own plumbing rather than a rule about temporary files. `php://temp`
WRAPS an inner memory stream and copies that stream's `eof` after every read. A line read
asks for a whole chunk, so filling the buffer drives the inner stream one read past its
last byte — the read that returns nothing and raises its `eof`. A sized `fread()` stops as
soon as it has what the caller asked for, and never makes that extra read.

So this reproduces the extra READ rather than guessing at its consequence: a line reader
that has emptied the holding area on a temp stream fills it once more. Bytes arriving keep
the stream open — that is the 9001-byte case, where the probe finds the next line already
in hand — and nothing arriving is the end. A seek still clears it, because a seek always
did.

It runs AFTER the line has been published, never before: the fill claims a concat window
of its own, and run while the line still held one it would build its chunk on top of the
line and hand back bytes that had moved.
